title: HMAC Final refuses CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE to prevent auth bypass — defend this
description: Why this choice is correct: after HmacUpdate(s) claimed the data (returned 0), wolfSSL's software HMAC state has no accumulated data. If Final returned CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE, the software fallback would compute HMAC over zero bytes and return a wrong MAC with no error. The code deliberately returns WC_HW_E at Final when the device lacks the algo (INIT fails with EOPNOTSUPP/ENOENT), trading a hard error for a silent auth bypass. What a future contributor might incorrectly change: 'why not fall back to software if hardware is unavailable at Final? That would be more resilient.' Answer: because the data was already consumed by Update — there is nothing for software to authenticate. Resilience here would mean silent wrong MACs.
